words.sense: Not allowing light to pass through a physical material.
misconceptions: Assuming material colour or thickness alone settles light transmission.
Confusing water resistance or privacy with stopping all light.

words.sense: Allowing some light through while blurring objects behind it.
misconceptions: Assuming blurred visibility means no light passes through.
Confusing water resistance or privacy with stopping all light.

semantic_axes.description: An opaque material blocks light; a translucent material passes some light but does not permit a clear view through it.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Nora’s wooden door?

beats.text: Nora switched on the hallway lamp, but no glow came through the closed wooden door.
beats.decisive_clue: the door transmitted no lamp light
beats.reason: The door transmitted no lamp light. Not allowing light to pass through a physical material.

beats.text: The door was painted pale yellow.
beats.decisive_clue: yellow paint does not change the observed failure to pass light
beats.reason: Yellow paint does not change the observed failure to pass light. Not allowing light to pass through a physical material.

chains.feedback_short: Yellow paint does not change the observed failure to pass light.
chains.feedback_deep: Opaque means not allowing light to pass through a physical material; translucent means allowing some light through while blurring objects behind it. Here, the door transmitted no lamp light. The new detail does not change the deciding fact: yellow paint does not change the observed failure to pass light. Thus opaque remains the stronger choice.
chains.contrast_rule: Opaque stops light; translucent lets light in but blurs the view.
